description: Provision an Azure Compute CapacityReservation via Azure Service Operator. Fields mirror the compute.azure.com/v1api20250401 CapacityReservation spec.

azureName.description:
AzureName: The name of the resource in Azure. This is often the same as the name of the resource in Kubernetes but it
doesn't have to be.

credentialFrom.description: Name of a Kubernetes Secret holding the Azure credential to use for this resource. Rendered as the serviceoperator.azure.com/credential-from annotation. Leave empty to inherit the credential from the namespace, then from the operator's global credential. The resource's subscription and resource group come from spec.owner, not from this field.

operatorSpec.description:
OperatorSpec: The specification for configuring operator behavior. This field is interpreted by the operator and not
passed directly to Azure

configMapExpressions.description: ConfigMapExpressions: configures where to place operator written dynamic ConfigMaps (created with CEL expressions).

items.description:
DestinationExpression is a CEL expression and a destination to store the result in. The destination may
be a secret or a configmap. The value of the expression is stored at the specified location in
the destination.

annotations.description: Annotations is an optional set of annotations to apply to the destination resource.

key.description:
Key is the key in the ConfigMap or Secret being written to. If the CEL expression in Value returns a string
this is required to identify what key to write to. If the CEL expression in Value returns a map[string]string
Key must not be set, instead the keys written will be determined dynamically based on the keys of the resulting
map[string]string.

owner.description:
Owner: The owner of the resource. The owner controls where the resource goes when it is deployed. The owner also
controls the resources lifecycle. When the owner is deleted the resource will also be deleted. Owner is expected to be a
reference to a compute.azure.com/CapacityReservationGroup resource

name.description: This is the name of the Kubernetes resource to reference.

scheduleProfile.description:
ScheduleProfile: Defines the schedule for Block and Future capacity reservations. Specifies the schedule during which
capacity reservation is active and VM or VMSS resource can be allocated using reservation. For Block capacity
reservations, the scheduleProfile, start, and end fields are immutable after creation. Please refer to
https://aka.ms/blockcapacityreservation for more details. Minimum API version for Block capacity reservations:
2025-04-01. Future capacity reservations must use this property with only a start time, which can be changed until the
‘modifiableUntil’ time. Please refer to https://aka.ms/futurecapacityreservation for more details. Minimum API
version for Future capacity reservations: 2026-04-01.

end.description:
End: The required end date for Block capacity reservations. Must be after the start date, with a duration of either
1–14 whole days or 3–26 whole weeks. Example: 2025-06-28.

start.description:
Start: The required start date for Block or Future capacity reservations. Block capacity reservations: Must be today or
within 56 days in the future. For same-day scheduling, requests must be submitted before 11:30 AM UTC. Future capacity
reservations: Must be at least 7 days in the future, and maximum 6 months in the future. Minimum API version for Future
capacity reservations: 2026-04-01. Example: 2025-06-27, applicable for both Block and Future capacity reservations.

sku.description:
Sku: SKU of the resource for which capacity needs be reserved. The SKU name and capacity is required to be set.  For
Block capacity reservations, sku.capacity can only accept values 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64. Currently VM Skus with the
capability called 'CapacityReservationSupported' set to true are supported. When 'CapacityReservationSupported' is true,
the SKU capability also specifies the 'SupportedCapacityReservationTypes', which lists the types of capacity
reservations (such as Targeted or Block) that the SKU supports. Refer to List Microsoft.Compute SKUs in a region
(https://docs.microsoft.com/rest/api/compute/resourceskus/list) for supported values.

capacity.description: Capacity: Specifies the number of virtual machines in the scale set.

tier.description:
Tier: Specifies the tier of virtual machines in a scale set.
Possible Values:
Standard
Basic
